title: Memory Reactivation Levels Remain Unaffected by Anticipated Interference Experiment 2 Dataset
description: EEG dataset from a visual working memory experiment (Experiment 2) examining whether memory reactivation levels are affected by anticipated interference. Participants memorized 2 or 6 lateral objects, then performed either a dual task with distractors or a single fixation-only task during the delay, before selecting the cued object in a probe display. The data have been preprocessed; the preprocessing steps are described in the associated preprint and OSF repository (Experiment 2).
methods_description: Each trial began with a key press and a fixation dot (500-650 ms), followed by 2 or 6 lateral objects for 1250 ms with a central cue indicating which to memorize. After a 1000 ms delay, half the blocks presented 4 distractors (dual task, identify same-category object) and half showed fixation only (single task). Dual task accuracy feedback was given, followed by a probe with 2 objects where participants chose the cued object with arrow keys, then received feedback.
